cands.bio: Democrat and Tuscaloosa attorney who has represented Alabama House District 70 since 2006. A former Tuscaloosa County assistant district attorney, he is an associate city attorney for Tuscaloosa. He chaired the Alabama Democratic Party from 2019 to 2022.
cands.gaps: We found no documented statements or actions by England on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, H-1B or immigration enforcement, abortion, school choice or teacher pay. We found no documented stance on guns or on funding and pay for police. The sources we had do not describe any controversies, foreign ties or notable endorsements. We could not independently confirm his birthplace and upbringing beyond his own campaign site. Ballotpedia says he did not complete its candidate survey. Whether his job with the Tuscaloosa city attorney's office is current comes only from his campaign site.

qual.background: He has served in the Alabama House since 2006, about 20 years. Before that he was a Tuscaloosa County assistant district attorney. He has worked in the Tuscaloosa city attorney's office since 2004 and holds a J.D. from the University of Alabama (2002). He was Alabama Democratic Party chair from 2019 to 2022.
qual.why: He has two decades of legislative service plus a long legal career in prosecution and municipal law, which fits the rubric's top band. Committee seats and board memberships were not counted.

cands.bio: Republican candidate for Alabama House District 70 in 2026. Attorney with a law degree from the Birmingham School of Law, also a realtor and adjunct professor. Previously worked in hospitality, banking and real estate. Has not held elected office.
cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace, where he grew up, or the year he moved to Alabama. No voting record exists because he has not held office. We found no stated positions on data centers, development limits, out-of-state or foreign land buying, immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion, or vouchers and charters. His campaign site mentions strategic tax incentives and attracting manufacturing but says nothing specific on these topics. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him. No news coverage or controversies were found.

back-police-order.evidence: Says he stands firmly with law enforcement and first responders and will back resources for police, firefighters and EMS.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Supports a state lottery as a dedicated education funding source, which he says could increase teacher pay. His site does not mention vouchers or charters.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: Says a state lottery for education could reduce the burden on property taxpayers without raising taxes. He does not pledge to end homestead taxes.
